NEXTACTIVITY

Privacy policy for NextActivity

Updated: 1 September 2026

1. Project responsibility and contact

Timo Friedl and Levin Reicherzer are responsible for the NextActivity project and can be contacted for support and privacy inquiries. Support and privacy inquiries can be sent to nextactivity01@gmail.com. A private residential address is not published. Which additional provider and contact details are required for a public release must be clarified legally before a production release.

NextActivity does not require a user account, contains no advertising, and uses no analytics, tracking, or advertising SDKs. No crash reports are sent to a NextActivity server. Personal data is not sold or disclosed to third parties for advertising, profiling, or other independent purposes.

2. Purpose, audience, and important limits

The app calculates situation-based leisure suggestions. Release 1 is intended for adults aged 18 and over and is not offered or promoted as a children’s app.

NextActivity does not provide medical, therapeutic, diagnostic, emergency, or other safety-critical advice. Health, sleep, and activity values are used only to adjust non-binding leisure ideas. For health concerns, danger, or emergencies, contact qualified professionals or the appropriate emergency services.

3. Data stored permanently on the device

Day plans store only one local date per activity, an optional local time, position and status, and a privacy-safe activity snapshot. They contain no calendar, health, location, or provider data; an optional link to a local scheduled activity is only an internal ID. Day plans are exported as these local values, older exports without day plans remain valid, and imported links do not automatically create notifications or calendar changes. Day plans can be removed individually or together with all local data.

The device stores the language selection, settings for budget, transport, manual offline mode and optional history, local acceptance/rejection feedback, helpful/not-helpful ratings, hidden activities, favorites, custom activities, collections, scheduled activities, and onboarding status. Quality ratings contain only a privacy-safe local activity key, category, rating, and, where voluntarily selected, a fixed reason category; external place and event IDs are reduced to their type or category. The displayed overall, category, and reason metrics are calculated locally and are not transmitted separately. Custom activities contain the title, description, category, minimum duration, estimated cost, indoor/outdoor setting, activity level, and company you enter. Favorites contain activity ID, title, description, category, and minimum duration. Collections contain only a name chosen by you, a local creation timestamp, and local activity-ID assignments; they do not copy location, health, calendar, or provider data. For an event favorite you explicitly save, a local snapshot also contains its origin, start time, duration, venue, provider name, availability status and, where present, its public HTTPS event page. Scheduled activities additionally contain time, reminder status and, where selected, a place name.

For adaptive sorting performed exclusively on the device, NextActivity stores learning events with a privacy-safe activity key; coarse activity features such as category, indoor/outdoor setting, strenuousness, movement type, duration and cost bands, broad location and company types, and source type; and coarse situation features such as day period, weekend status, broad location type, energy, company, hunger, and weather condition. If you explicitly select preferences, indoor/outdoor setting, intensity, mood, and flexible or banded duration and budget are also stored as coarse intent features. Each event includes the outcome, UTC timestamp, and provenance; provenance distinguishes an impression, direct selection, explicit feedback, favorite, planning, completion, and migrated legacy data. These entries contain no activity titles or descriptions, addresses, coordinates, exact time, duration, budget, weather, step, exercise, or sleep values, calendar details, or external provider identifiers. The learning model is evaluated deterministically on the device and uses no NextActivity server, external AI model, or telemetry.

Exact situation values, session permissions, search addresses, exact device coordinates, routes, events that have not been favorited, and calendar, health, and sleep values are not stored permanently by NextActivity. They remain only in memory for the current session; only the coarse context and intent categories of the learning model described above persist. As a limited caching exception, the app stores up to 24 lists of public places already found: current for 30 minutes and retained for no more than seven days as a stale immediate result. The cache key contains only a search grid rounded to about 110 metres and the language; entries contain public place data including place coordinates, name, category, distance, opening information, and indoor/outdoor classification, but no exact device coordinates or routes. The place cache is not exported and is removed when all local data is deleted. Optional history is disabled by default, limited to 100 entries, and stores only the activity, time, and, where already selected in the session, a place name.

Data management creates a versioned JSON export locally only when you explicitly request it and can import it again after a preview. Schema 4 contains settings, favorites, collections, hidden items, local learning and quality feedback including coarse features, provenance, and outcome, plans, and custom activities; history is included only after your explicit selection. Health values, coordinates, calendar content, session permissions, keys, and diagnostics are excluded; learning and quality feedback and collections contain no external place or event identifiers. NextActivity does not upload this export. Imported plans do not enable notifications automatically.

You can independently reset helpful/not-helpful ratings in Settings. This removes only learning events originating from explicit feedback; effects from direct selections, favorites, planning, and completions, as well as favorites, collections, history, plans, custom activities, and general app settings, remain. You can also reset all learning signals or reset them only for one activity or category. Other local data can be removed there selectively or by deleting the app or its app data. There is no cloud synchronization and no user account.

4. Optional device sources and permissions

Only after explicit permission for the current session does NextActivity read precise device location, the next relevant calendar appointment, today’s steps and exercise duration, or latest sleep duration. Location is used for weather, nearby places, and road routes. You can revoke operating-system permissions in system settings; manual input remains available without them.

The optional Android Focus & app pauses feature is disabled by default. If you enable it yourself and grant special accessibility access, NextActivity detects only switches to apps you selected. The service does not read text or other screen content and does not perform touches or input. App selection, daily allowances, focus end time, temporary exceptions, and measured usage duration are stored locally only and are not transmitted. You can disable the feature in NextActivity or revoke access in Android system settings at any time.

For new plans, you can choose whether they remain only in NextActivity, whether the app asks each time about adding a calendar event, or whether they are written automatically to one selected target calendar. The planning mode and the target calendar identifier and name are stored locally only and are not exported. NextActivity writes only to that exact calendar and does not silently fall back to another one if it becomes unavailable.

Calendar and Health Connect/HealthKit data are processed on the device. Steps, exercise duration, and sleep data are not sent to NextActivity servers or to the weather, place, or routing services named below. Public address lookup for an appointment location is disabled in release 1; a destination position already available on the device may be used for an OSRM route after permission.

When you enable a local reminder, NextActivity only then asks for notification permission and, on supported Android versions, revocable exact-alarm special access. Exact-to-the-second delivery is not guaranteed. The notification contains the title, description and, where stored locally, the place name of the scheduled activity.

5. Direct external services used after permission

The current release does not use the existing opt-in NextActivity backend proxy deployment and instead runs in direct mode. For a voluntary address search, the app sends the entered address or postal code directly to nominatim.openstreetmap.org. For a permitted weather request, the app sends coordinates rounded to approximately two decimal places and the requested weather fields directly to api.open-meteo.com. With location permission, more precise coordinates, the search radius, and OSM object filters are sent to overpass-api.de and, only after an error or unusable result, to overpass.private.coffee for nearby places. Start and destination coordinates and the mode of transport are sent directly to routing.openstreetmap.de for road routes. Public transport times are estimated locally only.

All configured network addresses use HTTPS. External images from arbitrary OSM image tags are disabled. The services also necessarily receive the IP address and standard connection data. Open-Meteo states that troubleshooting logs may contain coordinates and are deleted after 90 days. Private.coffee describes truncated IP addresses and log retention of up to 48 hours. FOSSGIS states that route requests are stored in server log files; its current notice does not specify a concrete retention period. The providers’ current notices remain authoritative.

6. Public website and email contact

The public privacy and contact site is intended to be hosted on GitHub Pages. According to GitHub’s documentation, GitHub logs a visitor’s IP address for security purposes and processes further usage and connection data under its privacy statement. The website generated by NextActivity itself sets no cookies, includes no analytics, and loads no fonts, scripts, or images from third-party hosts.

If you voluntarily email nextactivity01@gmail.com, the email providers involved, including Google as the provider for this address, process your sender address, technical message information, and the content you choose to send. The message is used only to handle your inquiry. Do not send health data, location data, or other sensitive content that is not necessary for your request.

7. Disabled sources and attribution

Google Places, Google place photos, and Ticketmaster live events are not enabled or configured without a dedicated backend proxy. Manual events remain available. There is also no live occupancy, live traffic, or public-transport timetable source; the app does not simulate such data.

Weather data: Open-Meteo (open-meteo.com, CC BY 4.0). Map and place data: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and Overpass. Routing: FOSSGIS/OSRM (routing.openstreetmap.de). Map issues can be reported at openstreetmap.org/fixthemap.

8. Retention, deletion, and inquiries

Session data and short app-side caches for weather and routes exist only in memory and are discarded when the relevant permission is revoked or no later than when the app closes. The local place cache described in section 3 is discarded after no more than seven days and removed when all local data is deleted. The server-side retention described above is controlled by the respective external providers.

The adaptive learning model retains at most 1,000 learning events and no event for longer than 730 days. Time weighting causes short-term signals to lose influence substantially sooner. A full learning reset deletes all learning events; an activity or category reset deletes only the selected scope, and resetting helpful/not-helpful ratings deletes only events with explicit-feedback provenance.

Favorites, collections, custom activities, scheduled activities, and history can be deleted in the app. Data management can remove all NextActivity data stored permanently on the device, including the learning model. Because there is no NextActivity account or cloud storage, no account deletion is required.

Send requests concerning access, correction, deletion, restriction, data portability, or objection to Timo Friedl and Levin Reicherzer at nextactivity01@gmail.com. Where processing is based on permission, you can withdraw it with future effect. You may also contact the competent data protection supervisory authority.
